newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EDP telecoms activity may help shares.
newsitem.headline: EDP telecoms activity may help shares.

text.p: The present share price of utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal is fair but if the group enters the telecommunications sector there may be greater short- and medium-term interest in the stock, according to a study by Spanish bank Argentaria.
The study for June-July rated EDP as "neutral," meaning that the utility is expected to trade in line with the market over the next few months.
"EDP is very well positioned to enter the telecommunications business, taking into account its present infrastructure," it said.
EDP has said it plans to apply for a third mobile telephone licence in Portugal.

"EDP seems to be fairly priced by a discounted cash flow analysis. A market multiples comparison, namely with the Spanish utilities, shows that EDP is trading at slightly higher levels, which nevertheless may be justified by lower levels of competition," said the report.

"EDP has been consolidating the current level of prices and is unlikely to outperform the market in the very short term. However, the group's likely entry into the telecommunications business and the interest in EDP already demonstrated by some Spanish companies may bring additional interest in the short-to-medium term, which is not included in the discounted cash flow analysis or in the market multiples comparison," said the Argentaria report.
Argentaria forecasted that EDP's end of year profits will be 90.328 billion escudos, rising to 99.101 billion escudos in 1998 and 105.569 billion escudos in 1999.
EDP was responsible for 81 percent of the electricity produced in Portugal in 1996.
In afternoon trade, EDP's share price was steady at 3,320 escudos in volume of 1,077,249 shares.
